annotations.description: Only 2 of 3 brokers are reachable; the cluster tolerates one loss.

diagnosis.summary: Broker lakehouse-dual-role-0 is Running/Ready but its metrics endpoint is unreachable, keeping the KafkaBrokerDown alert firing. 60 partitions remain under-replicated and active_controller count reads 0. The root cause is a Chaos Mesh experiment deployed ~133 minutes ago that caused all three brokers (and Flink) to terminate (exit 255/Unknown); broker-0 has not fully rejoined since—likely a lingering network fault from the experiment.
diagnosis.root_cause: A Chaos Mesh experiment (chaos-mesh-local revision 9187ff9e9e6f, deployed ~133 min ago) caused all Kafka broker pods, the kafka-exporter, kafka-admin, and Flink pods to terminate with exit code 255 (Unknown) at approximately the same instant. Brokers 1 and 2 recovered fully. Broker-0 (lakehouse-dual-role-0, node lakehouse-worker2) is Kubernetes-Ready but its Prometheus metrics endpoint cannot be scraped, indicating it is network-isolated rather than crashed—consistent with a surviving Chaos Mesh NetworkChaos or PodChaos rule still targeting that pod or node. The 60 under-replicated partitions and the active_controllers metric reading 0 (broker-0 is likely the KRaft active controller, but its metric feed is blocked) confirm broker-0 is not fully reachable by the cluster. Per runbook, restarting the pod will not fix a network-layer fault and would destroy evidence; the network/chaos fault must be resolved first.
diagnosis.impact: The Kafka cluster is operating with 2 of 3 brokers fully reachable. With RF=3 and min.insync.replicas=2, writes are still served, but there is zero fault-tolerance margin: one more broker loss will stall all producers. 60 partitions are under-replicated. Consumer lag for the Flink job is 200 messages; Flink itself is healthy and checkpointing normally, so lag will drain once replication recovers.

evidence.finding: All 3 broker pods Running/Ready, but brokers_scraped_up shows lakehouse-dual-role-0=false. under_replicated_partitions=60, under_min_isr_partitions=0, offline_partitions=0, active_controllers=0. Consumer lag (flink-events-to-iceberg)=200.

lakehouse-dual-role-0, dual-role-1, dual-role-2, kafka-admin, kafka-exporter all show last_termination reason=Unknown exit_code=255 finished_minutes_ago~129—a simultaneous multi-pod kill ~129 min ago consistent with Chaos Mesh.

chaos-mesh-local was deployed with revision 9187ff9e9e6f ~133 min ago (immediately before the mass pod-kill), then updated again to c3f9dacefde3 ~82 min ago and 47886843e767 ~15 min ago, suggesting ongoing chaos experiment activity.
Flink job RUNNING/STABLE, started 127.9 min ago (restarted after the same chaos event). 28.23 completed checkpoints in last 5 min, 0 failed. Consumer lag 200.
All nodes Ready, no pressure, no cordons—node failure is ruled out as the cause.
Runbook docs/runbooks/kafka.md#kafkabrokerdown: broker Running+Ready but metrics not scraped = network-isolated, not crashed. Do NOT restart—escalate to network/chaos owner.
chaos-mesh-local Synced/Healthy on latest revision 47886843e767; all other apps Synced/Healthy—no gitops issue.

proposed_action.rationale: Broker-0 is network-isolated (Kubernetes-Ready but metrics unreachable), which the runbook explicitly identifies as a network-layer fault rather than a pod crash. Restarting the pod would not fix the network fault and would destroy ISR and connection-error evidence. The fault correlates directly with Chaos Mesh experiment deployments; a human with access to Chaos Mesh must inspect and delete any active NetworkChaos/PodChaos resources targeting broker-0 or lakehouse-worker2 before the broker can rejoin.

follow_ups: Inspect and delete any active Chaos Mesh experiments (NetworkChaos, PodChaos, etc.) targeting namespace kafka or node lakehouse-worker2—`kubectl get networkchaos,podchaos -A` and check chaos-mesh dashboard.
Verify broker-0 rejoins the ISR and under_replicated_partitions drops to 0 after the network fault is cleared.
Confirm active_controllers returns to 1 once broker-0 metrics are scrapeable again.
Chaos Mesh was re-deployed ~15 min ago (revision 47886843e767); verify whether a new experiment is in progress or if this was a configuration-only change.
Consider adding a runbook step or alert annotation that links KafkaBrokerDown to active Chaos Mesh experiments to accelerate future triage.
Consumer lag of 200 should drain automatically once broker-0 is healthy; monitor and confirm.
